name: Phone Cases
description: Size the market for smartphone protective cases.
formula: TAM = Population x Penetration_rate x Purchase_frequency x Average_spend
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify addressable population = target_population x addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply penetration rate = addressable_population x penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate annual spend per user = purchase_frequency x avg_spend_per_purchase
Step 4: Calculate TAM = penetrating_users x annual_spend_per_user
key_insight: The addressable segment (who actually buys a case) matters more than raw population here -- most smartphone owners exist, but not all of them buy one, and that filter is the real sizing lever.
common_mistakes: Sizing all smartphone owners instead of the subset who actually buy cases
Using a penetration rate that assumes a large share of an already crowded, low-differentiation category
Forgetting purchase frequency -- cases are bought more than once a year for many buyers, not as a one-time purchase
framework_soundbite: Smartphone owners who actually buy cases, buying more than once a year, in a crowded category -- penetration should stay modest.
business_contexts: an accessories brand evaluating entry into the phone case market
a retailer sizing demand for a private-label phone case line
question_patterns: A consumer accessories brand is deciding whether to launch a phone case line and wants to size the annual market opportunity first.

prompts.beginner: Estimate the total addressable market for smartphone protective cases.
prompts.intermediate: A consumer accessories brand is deciding whether to launch a phone case line and wants to size the annual market opportunity first.
prompts.advanced: A private-label accessories manufacturer has been offered exclusive shelf space by a major retailer, contingent on committing to a phone case line within the quarter. Leadership needs a credible size-of-prize estimate before agreeing to the terms.

approach_guidance.top_down_why: Start from smartphone owners, narrow to the segment that actually buys cases, apply penetration, then multiply by purchase frequency and price -- narrowing down from the device install base.
approach_guidance.bottom_up_why: Or start from one case-buying customer: their annual spend (cases/year x price), then scale up by how many of them this brand penetrates. Both reach the same number from opposite directions.
